chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi' from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Abu Sa'd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Shaving (the head) is obligatory upon three types of people: a man who performed partial shaving (tabdil), a man who performed an optional (nafl) Hajj without having performed it before, and a man who cut his hair (during Ihram).

key_terms.عَقَصَ: cut hair (specifically in a way that incurs penalty)

ai.seo_question: What are the three cases where shaving the head is obligatory for a man in Ihram?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to clarify the specific conditions triggering the mandatory shaving (halq) of the entire head as expiation for a male pilgrim in Ihram. The text distinguishes between the penalty for partial cutting (taqsir) versus full shaving, the unique requirement for those performing an optional Hajj (Hajj al-Nadf) who have not previously performed the obligatory Hajj, and the general rule for cutting hair. This highlights the juristic precision in Shia fiqh regarding the gradation of penalties based on the nature of the violation and the pilgrim's status.
